problem: 'proposes a few hundred candidate boxes' contradicts Section 2, which correctly says selective search gives about 2000 proposals per image. A student may carry the wrong number into an exam.
fix: Say 'proposes a few thousand candidate boxes (about 2000 from selective search) and keeps only the best after suppression', or drop the number from the lead.

problem: The labelling rule is incomplete. The standard rule also makes the anchor with the highest IoU against each ground-truth box positive, so every object gets at least one positive anchor. Without this, a student can believe an object whose best anchor has IoU 0.6 gets no positive anchor at all.
fix: Add: 'The anchor with the highest IoU for a given ground-truth box is also labelled positive, even if that IoU is below 0.7, so every object has at least one positive anchor.'

problem: The loss as written lets background proposals contribute to L_box. In Fast R-CNN the box loss applies only to proposals that contain an object (c ≥ 1); background RoIs contribute only L_cls.
fix: Write L = L_cls + λ·[c ≥ 1]·L_box, and state that [c ≥ 1] is 1 for a proposal with an object class and 0 for background.

problem: The caption says the sharing (feature map used for both proposals and heads) is 'the speed gain over R-CNN'. Over R-CNN the gain is convolving the image once instead of 2000 times; sharing the map with the proposal network is the gain over Fast R-CNN.
fix: Say: 'Computing the feature map once, instead of once per crop, is the gain over R-CNN; reusing that same map for the RPN is the further gain over Fast R-CNN.'

problem: 'RoI Align ... is now the default in every RoI head' is an overstatement; many Faster R-CNN implementations still ship RoI pooling, and RoI Align became standard mainly in segmentation and recent detection codebases.
fix: Say: 'RoI Align from Mask R-CNN is now the usual choice in new RoI heads, especially where masks are predicted.'
